'At least double' has not happened ($3.43 to $5.33 is +55%) and is NOT drafted; 'multiple billions' is not drafted either. OPERATOR NOTE: Pieverse moved more than 30% inside 24 hours on November 22 (coin-research event window rule); re-check the Pieverse tweet against the live price before it posts.

Trestly launched kUSDT on Kaspa on November 15 2026: a KCC-20 covenant token on the Kaspa L1, backed by USDT locked in vaults on Ethereum or BNB Chain; three of five signers approve a mint or a release, four of five a rule change; a wallet to wallet transfer needs no signer. Product check (coin-research row 8): trestly.io and trestly.io/status return an app shell to a plain fetch (HTTP 200, 6,705 bytes, 'Loading Trestly'); /llms.txt, /api/status and /status.json are 404; the sitemap lists bridge, swap, pool, reserves, activity and network pages; the app bundle itself carries 'The deployment must list 5 signers' and 'Approved by {threshold} of {count} bridge signers', which confirms the five-signer design from the project's own code. The three of five threshold, the launch date and the audit status rest on dated coverage that quotes Trestly's own pages. No reserve, volume or user figure is printed (one monitor read put the float near 6,000 kUSDT on November 19: tiny, not printed). Copy: 'went live on November 15', 'You lock USDT in a vault on Ethereum and a dollar token gets minted on the Kaspa L1', 'three of the five have to approve'.

fact_check.verdict: verified on the project's own repository, project NOT named in copy. The kasperolabs/kozmic-bridge README: 'USDC between Ethereum and Kaspa L1, both ways, verified by zero-knowledge proofs alone'; live on mainnet in both directions since 2026-11-16 (a first instance ran with real USDC from 2026-11-15 and is closed to new deposits); a Kaspa covenant verifies a zero-knowledge proof of Ethereum's finality, and Ethereum verifies Kaspa's proof of work on the way back; no custodian, no multisig, no admin key, no pause function; 'New and not audited by a paid firm. Move only what you can afford to lose'. The Kaspa developer roundup of November 22 says the team published the code, tested moving real USDC and plans 'a few more rounds of testing before opening it to the public'. Copy therefore says 'on mainnet since November 16' and 'the team says it wants a few more rounds of testing before it opens it up to everybody', never that it is open to everybody. Not printed: Circle can freeze the Ethereum vault under USDC's own terms; the design reviews in the repository's docs folder were not read. 'Neither one has been audited by an outside firm yet' covers both bridges as each project states it.
fact_check.source: github.com/kasperolabs/kozmic-bridge and its raw README (fetched 2026-11-23); kucoin.com/news/insight/KAS/6b0337009278e40007d91222 (Kaspa dev roundup, November 22 2026, sourced to the Kaspa Unchained account on X)

fact_check.claim: 'we exited the bear market in September and we're in a new bear market... 11 weekly closes above the 200-day moving average... above the 50-week for like six weeks... we closed below it, and one week later we went below the 200-week... two bear markets and two crypto winters in the same year, nobody points it out' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified on Kraken XBTUSD daily candles, weeks closed on Sunday (my calc). Weekly closes above the 50-week SMA: September 20 2026 ($81,164 against $78,789) through November 1 ($78,239 against $75,731), seven closes across six weeks; before that Bitcoin had closed under it every week since early November 2025. It lost the line again on November 8 ($74,738 against $75,490), and the next weekly close, November 15 ($65,315), was under the 200-week SMA (around $68,400). The first close under the 200-week SMA this year came in June 2026 (Sunday close of June 28, $59,490 against around $62,800). Weekly closes above the 200-day SMA: August 23 through November 8, twelve by this data (Mike said 11; not printed). So the first bear market by Mike's rule ran from November 2025 to September 2026, the second began in November 2026, and Bitcoin has closed under its 200-week SMA in two separate stretches of 2026. Copy: 'closed back above its 50-week SMA in September and held it for around six weeks', 'In early November it lost the 50-week SMA again', 'One week later it closed under the 200-week SMA, for the second time this year', 'two bear markets and two crypto winters inside the same year' (his words; crypto winter is his name for trading under the 200-week SMA). 'Never happened before' is not claimed. $BTC is $61,240 at drafting, -5.9% on 7 days, 51.4% under its $126,080 all-time high; no price is printed.
fact_check.source: api.kraken.com/0/public/OHLC pair=XBTUSD interval=1440 and interval=10080 (read 2026-11-23); api.coingecko.com coins/markets (2026-11-23); schedule-tweets/data/yt-text-polls.json (September 21 2026 poll: first close above the 50-week SMA in 45 weeks)

yt_posts.topic: Two bridges brought dollars onto Kaspa within days of each other (USDT with three of five signers, USDC with zero-knowledge proofs and no signers): what is live, what is still missing, and why Mike likes that it is happening at the bottom
yt_posts.body_style: news hook, the recap of his own question, bridge one, bridge two, the caveat, the timing, the comment ask
yt_posts.body:
Two bridges that bring dollars onto Kaspa went live within days of each other, and almost nobody noticed. One is for USDT, one is for USDC, and they work in completely different ways. Here's what's actually there, and why I'm glad it's happening now.

Quick recap. In mid-November I asked why Kaspa needs its own dollar instead of just USDT and USDC. The best answer I got back was that bringing USDT over means trusting a bridge, and a bridge is one more thing that can break.

Well, the bridges showed up. Both of them sit on the Kaspa L1 itself, on the covenants that went live in June.

The first one went live on November 15. You lock USDT in a vault on Ethereum and a dollar token gets minted on the Kaspa L1. Five signers stand behind it, and three of the five have to approve before anything gets minted or released.

The second one takes USDC, and it has no signers at all. No custodian, no admin key. Kaspa itself checks a zero-knowledge proof that your deposit is final on Ethereum, and Ethereum checks Kaspa's proof of work on the way back. It has been on mainnet since November 16, and the team says it wants a few more rounds of testing before it opens it up to everybody.

Here's the thing: neither one has been audited by an outside firm yet. And to me the whole setup is still a little overly complex. We don't want to have to think about any of this. We want to rest assured that it works and that we can trust it.

That's why I like the timing. This is the bottom. $KAS is around 2.6 cents and nobody's around. This is exactly when you want the tech built, tested and audited, so that when everybody comes flooding back into crypto, nobody gets to say Kaspa doesn't have this, or it wasn't audited, or you have to jump through an extra hoop.

We're getting there. Never financial advice.

So tell me: which one would you trust with your own dollars, the bridge with five signers or the one that runs on zero-knowledge proofs with no signers at all? Or neither until the audits are done? Drop it in the comments.

If this caught you up on what's getting built on Kaspa, hit like and subscribe for more.
